correctness.rationale: The exact equivalence J(n,2)-v = L(K_n-ab) reduces all total dominating sets to selected-edge graphs with no K2 component and at most one isolate, or precisely isolates a,b. Labelled exponential decomposition gives the h_j polynomial and the edge-transitive deletion derivative gives the full polynomial. For m selected edges, c nontrivial components, q cycle rank and r incident labels, r=m+c-q<=m+floor(m/2); this proves the lower bound. Each residue class forces the listed acyclic tree component types, and constructions attain the bound for all n>=4. Cayley tree counts and the incidence double count establish every minimizer formula. The independent direct-graph checker reproduces every coefficient for n=4..7 and the exact first nonzero coefficient for n=8,9. Infinite statements are proved combinatorially, not inferred from those tests.

originality.rationale: The closest research paper (arXiv:2610.04675, Theorem 14) determines the scalar total domination number on the UNDELETED J(n,2), while previously published OEIS A304561 and A303048 give counts for undeleted graphs. A related recoverable claim also classifies undeleted optimizers. The present one-vertex-deleted graph has an additional two-isolate family, a distinct full cardinality polynomial, and different minimum/optimizer counts; those conclusions are not supplied by the undeleted source statements or numerical tables. Literature and mathematical-record searches under equivalent line-graph and total-edge-domination formulations found no covering result. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: Vertex deletion is a canonical robustness operation on an edge-transitive graph family. The new object has an exact entire total-domination polynomial for every n>=4, not merely a scalar optimum. Its sharp mod-3 sensitivity and exhaustive forest structure/count of minimum sets expose the two-isolate families that are impossible in the original graph. These precise parameters are motivated by how a single missing Johnson vertex changes allowable total domination; the all-size distribution is independently useful for exact enumerative questions. The previously published intact-graph counts are identified as prior and are not the asserted new result.
